note: Multiple primary studies identify hyperventilation as a key characteristic phenotypic feature of dominant RNU2-2-related DEE119.

evidence.text: In a cohort of patients with RNU2-2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, hyperventilation was specifically identified in 3 out of 5 patients alongside obstructive sleep apnea and status epilepticus.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3).

evidence.text: Recurrent de novo mutations in RNU2-2 define a neurodevelopmental disorder and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by intellectual disability, microcephaly, hypotonia, epilepsy, and hyperventilation.

source.title: Mutations in the small nuclear RNA gene RNU2-2 cause a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with prominent epilepsy
source.quote: The disorder is characterized by intellectual disability, autistic behavior, microcephaly, hypotonia, epilepsy and hyperventilation.
